players.product: Neoverse V2/V3 CPU core IP and CSS compute subsystems

quarterly_data.signal: Arm's 20-F (fiscal year ended March 31, 2026) customer concentration: its top five customers (including Arm China and SoftBank Group) collectively accounted for approximately 57% of total revenue in fiscal 2026 (56% in fiscal 2025, 54% in fiscal 2024), and its largest customer individually, Arm China, accounted for approximately 16% (17% and 21% in the two prior years). Three customers collectively represented 42% of fiscal 2026 revenue (largest 16%, second 14%, third 12%). Arm China acts as Arm's commercial conduit to the PRC market; revenue from related parties (Arm China, equity-method investees and SoftBank Group-controlled entities) was $1,499 million (30% of revenue) vs $823 million in fiscal 2025, with related-party license and other revenue $1,009 million vs $418 million (+141%).
quarterly_data.figure: top five customers approximately 57%; Arm China approximately 16%; related-party revenue $1,499 million (30%)

quarterly_data.signal: Arm's 20-F revenue by line for fiscal 2026: license and other revenue $2,307 million vs $1,839 million (+25%), driven by continued strong demand for Arm IP, the timing and size of multiple high-value license agreements and contributions from backlog; royalty revenue $2,613 million vs $2,168 million (+21%). XBRL: License and Other Revenue $2.31B (+25.4% YoY), Royalty Revenue $2.61B (+20.5% YoY).
quarterly_data.figure: license and other $2,307 million (+25%); royalty $2,613 million (+21%)

quarterly_data.signal: Arm's 20-F: as of March 31, 2026 the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations was $2,071.4 million (potential future royalties excluded); Arm expects to recognize approximately 28% of it as revenue over the next 12 months, 21% over the subsequent 13-to-24-month period and the remainder thereafter. Contract liabilities rose to $1,046 million from $911 million, with $581 million of customer prepayments and billings in advance during the year.

Arm's 20-F on production silicon: its risk factors state that the entry into production silicon (the Arm AGI CPU) brings dependence on third-party foundry partners and contract manufacturers, upfront purchase obligations for wafer supply, packaging and testing services, and supply chain dependencies on memory suppliers, packaging vendors and system integrators. Arm also recently entered into an agreement to arrange for certain semiconductor products to be supplied by a third party to a customer, with purchase commitments of approximately $100 million to be purchased over the next 12 months, and expects its purchase commitments are likely to grow materially in subsequent years. Purchases of property and equipment were $545 million in fiscal 2026 vs $219 million in fiscal 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: purchase commitments approximately $100 million over next 12 months; property and equipment purchases $545 million vs $219 million

quarterly_data.signal: Arm's 20-F: in January 2025 SoftBank Group announced the Stargate Project, a joint venture between SoftBank Group, OpenAI and Oracle to build new AI infrastructure, where Arm was named a key technology partner; Arm states it has received no formal commitments that its technology will be used.

Arm's 20-F: on August 26, 2025 Arm completed the sale of its Artisan foundation IP business (standard cell libraries, memory compilers and general-purpose I/Os) to Cadence Design Systems under an agreement entered into in April 2025; Arm and Cadence provide each other transition support services for up to 18 months after completion.

connects_to.relationship: Arm architecture licensed for the Dragonfly C1000 AI data-center CPU

contracts.signal: Arm's 20-F describes Qualcomm as currently a major customer that accounted for 9% of Arm's total revenue for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, while the two remain in litigation over Qualcomm's Architecture License Agreement and Technology License Agreement; that case is expected to go to trial in the fourth calendar quarter of 2026.

connects_to.relationship: Technology licensing and design services agreement supporting SoftBank's AI compute build-out

contracts.signal: Arm's 20-F: revenue from the licensing and servicing arrangements under the Consulting Agreement with SoftBank Group was $704.4 million in fiscal 2026 vs $145.5 million in fiscal 2025, and Arm held current contract assets of $645.8 million from a SoftBank Group affiliate at March 31, 2026. During fiscal 2026 one statement of work was restructured into a fixed payment of $300 million, to be paid during the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027; Arm may also be entitled to royalty fees under certain statements of work, on terms to be negotiated later.
contracts.value: $704.4 million fiscal 2026 revenue (fiscal 2025: $145.5 million); $300 million fixed payment in fiscal 2027
contracts.date_signed: Consulting Agreement dated August 21, 2023; statements of work entered into and amended during the fiscal years ended March 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024

contracts.signal: Arm's 20-F: SoftBank Group acquired all of Ampere in November 2025; Arm continues to have licensing and servicing arrangements with Ampere and recognized revenue of $3.6 million from Ampere in fiscal 2026 ($3.5 million in fiscal 2025, $49.3 million in fiscal 2024).
